chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Can a believer have ten shirts?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Twenty?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Thirty?' He said: 'Yes. This is not extravagance. Extravagance is when you use your best-preserved garment as your everyday work wear.'

key_terms.السَّرَف: Extravagance, wastefulness (israf) — the forbidden practice of wasting or misusing resources
key_terms.ثَوْبُ بِذْلَتِكَ: Your everyday/work garment — clothing worn for daily manual labor or rough use
key_terms.ثَوْبُ صَوْنِكَ: Your preserved/best garment — clothing kept for formal occasions or to protect its quality

ai.seo_question: Is it extravagance (israf) to own many shirts in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the Islamic concept of extravagance (israf) in clothing. He affirms that owning many shirts — even thirty — is permissible for a believer. The true extravagance is wearing one's fine, well-preserved garment for rough daily work, thereby ruining it rather than caring for one's possessions properly. This teaching reflects the Imam's emphasis on practical wisdom in managing one's belongings.
